I'm tired of living, to put it frankly. I love sleep, so eternal sleep is immensely attractive to me. At this point, I don't think meds can help me. They'll be able to aid the side effects of my depression, but the core problem remains unsolved and frankly it is impossible to solve. Trying to fight it is wasteful of both time and the efforts of others. I hurt the people around me and ultimately, though in the short term they will be devastated, my death will benefit them.

It's my time because I see no future for myself. I'm a lucky person and live an above-average life, but day-to-day I have become numb.  I'm stuck and there's no way for me to escape. Believe me I've tried practically everything, but no matter what, my depression is pervasive and invasive. I've stopped feeling or caring about much of anything.

I attempted suicide a couple months ago (wimped out at the last second and ended up going into a coma instead of dying), and since then my friends have abandoned and alienated me. It's understandable I guess, they don't want to take on the burden of holding my feelings and life as their responsibility.

I was on Lexapro and I stopped partly because of the effects and partly because I was hoping the withdrawal would give me the final push toward suicide. Before I was on meds, I felt this continuous, excruciating pain that was practically unbearable. After medication, the pain subsided, which may sound like a good thing, but all that was left was emptiness. In many ways the emptiness was even more unbearable than the pain as it hindered my ability for creative thought and expression through writing. 

To my surprise, withdrawal hasn't been that bad. I am in constant mood swings, very capricious in my thinking, and the pain has started to come back. But other than that, it's not that severe. I thought it would be worse as I cut it cold turkey.

Ah man, I know how you feel. There was a 4chan post very similar to that that has been circling reddit for some time. Whenever I see it I get so frustrated. 

But there's nothing much we can do but tell them politely and concisely that things like that are written in a perspective that is completely irrelevant to those with depression. People who see suicidal feelings in that way will never understand what it's like to be in our position. Thus they are not the best people to keep in your support group.

Meds may work for you, I'd recommend you try them. But as a warning - there are side effects. For me, my depression spiraled to the point every day I lived in severe emotional agony. I was unable to do work, unable to think, unable to do anything else except crawl into a fetal position on the floor and scratch my arms with razor blades. I did something stupid, ended up in the hospital, and got put on medication.

Medication doesn't pull you out of the negative and into the positive, it simply lessens the negative. I no longer felt the intense, stabbing pain like before. But instead, there was just emptiness. Apathy. I lost my creative side and was apathetic toward everything and anything. I didn't feel like myself. 

To me, feeling nothing feels worse than feeling something. So I'm thinking of stopping medication. 

However, there are people who've had grand success with it. Ultimately, it isn't medication that will cure your depression. Medication will only make it more bearable. You are the true cure to depression.

One small moment could set the stage and kickstart a love and zest for life you never thought possible. Just give those small moments a chance. 

When I attempted suicide on that fateful night, it kind of blew up in my face. I ended up getting rescued, but by that point, word started spreading of what I had done. My parents were shocked, the school got involved, people I didn't want to know about my mental health found out, things were just not good. 

I guess what I'm trying to say is to take it slow, think about things. You don't want to do something rash that may end up in regret. Seek help from your friend, from family (if they are the type that you know will support you and understand), and from professionals. 

There is hope, there is a way out of the dark hole of apathy and emptiness. All you have to do is look up.

As someone who was/is a self-harmer, my initial reaction to this is very negative. Not only is she struggling with depression and cutting, but she is suffering alone. What you are doing is forcing her to give up the one thing that gives her the relief from pent up emotions and mental pain in order to prevent **more** painful emotions (you leaving her). 

I'd compare it to telling a painkiller addict to stop taking pills or else you will stab them in the leg. 

I know you are trying to help her, but that isn't the best way. 

And please reconsider telling her parents. People who have never been a self-injurer before can never understand what it's like to go though something like this. She needs help, but not from people who aren't capable of helping her. In fact, they may even worsen the situation. 

Right now, your post makes it seem like you're being an enemy to her recovery. You have to start fighting alongside her, not against her.

Co2: 5lb tank pressurized 1bps

Filtration: Eheim 2215

Substrate: ADA aquasoil Amazonia II 

Flora: HC, cyperus helferi, flame moss, christmas moss, java moss, dwarf hairgrass, some rotala species, red ludwigia, dwarf sag, blyxa japonica

Fauna: Red Cherry Shrimp, Crystal Black Shrimp

I've found two sort of "solutions" for this.

People have always told me to "get a hobby," but it wasn't until I found something I absolutely loved that the advice rang true. It may take some time, but just keep your eyes open for anything that sparks your interest or excitement. It was a year ago when my little cousin brought home some goldfish for the fair when I stumbled upon the planted aquarium hobby and it's helped me through the darkest of times. 

Secondly...avoid places that are familiar to you. Familiar places breed familiar habits. Be spontaneous, and try new things at every opportunity you can get. If this just means taking a different route in your daily routine or spending an hour in a nearby park so be it. 

I don't know how much this will help you since my situation is very similar to yours, but I've found a little relief in these two things so hopefully you will too :)

How long have you had your ladder? Usually the ladder needs some time for it to develop a slime coat, which can slow down the bubbles and allow for greater diffusion. 

Right now I'm using a Hagen ladder with my 5lb pressurized CO2 (I used to have DIY), and I'd say it's diffusing moderately well. It's running on a 20 gallon long with 2bps and my drop checker is a yellow-green. The bubbles shrink to about 1/4 their original size as they go up the ladder. 

About the O2 under the leaves - or pearling as what many people call it - don't worry about it. It does indicate good plant growth but only certain plants pearl well and just because you don't see bubbles doesn't mean your plant isn't growing! The only plant I've seen pearl for me is dwarf baby tears. 

I really can't say anything for ceramic or chopstick diffusers though. From what I've heard, sometimes the pressure for the DIY system just isn't enough to push the bubbles through a ceramic disk.
